All six items have an answer. Sourced facts are marked "Sourced" and my reading is marked "Inference". The Claude Code docs were read on 2026-11-04 and the CLI version they cover is not stated.

## 1. Plugin `agent` key and claude.ai cloud sessions
Sourced:
- A plugin may ship a root `settings.json`. Only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` are honored, and unknown keys are ignored. `agent` makes one of the plugin's agents the main thread, with its system prompt, tool restrictions and model. This is quoted from the "Create plugins" page, via https://agentpatterns.ai/tools/claude/plugin-main-agent-override-and-path-injection/. That page also says the key needs Claude Code v2.1.157 or later. I did not read the official page directly.
- Other mechanisms: `claude --agent <name>` starts a session where the main thread takes on that agent's prompt, tools and model, and overrides the `agent` setting (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents). Neither can be set from inside a cloud session.
- Cloud sessions do not install plugins that the repo's `.claude/settings.json` turns on, including `extraKnownMarketplaces` entries. They also skip plugins enabled only in user settings. Only plugins from server-managed settings arrive. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/install ("Cloud session" tab), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org.
- The repo's own `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/` and `.claude/settings.json` hooks and permission rules do load in cloud sessions, in a session with one repository (cloud-environments).
- Conflict: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/88214 quotes an older docs line saying repo-declared plugins install at session start. The current docs say they do not. The same issue shows managed-settings plugins also failed to install at startup on CLI 2.1.296. A reported workaround is `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL=1` in the managed-settings `env` block. That comes from the issue thread, not the docs.
- https://claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support lists plugin `settings` as "Loads" in Claude Code and "Ignored" in Chat and Cowork. It has no cloud row.

Inference:
- A plugin-shipped `agent` will not reliably take effect in a claude.ai cloud session, because the plugin itself may not be installed there.
- I found no documented way for a plugin to force the main-thread agent in cloud sessions.
- Not verified: whether an `agent` key in the repo's own `.claude/settings.json` is honored in the cloud. Repo settings hooks do load, so it may work, but the docs I read do not say so.
- B2 should assume the session-start context must carry the root rules.

## 2. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` expansion
Sourced:
- Expanded in skill, command and agent markdown bodies ("anywhere in the Markdown body", substituted inline when the content loads). Also expanded in hook and monitor commands, in MCP and LSP server config, and in skill `allowed-tools` Bash rules. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.
- On the skills page, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` are "substituted only in plugin skills".
- It is not in the environment of commands run through the Bash tool, in the main session or in a subagent (manifest-reference). Hook, MCP and LSP processes do get it exported.
- The docs say nothing about text passed as a subagent prompt or a brief.

Inference: a literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in a brief, or in text the root writes at run time, is not expanded. Only the root's own loaded agent or skill body expands it. The root must substitute the absolute path itself, or `holyagent.md` can contain the variable so that its loaded body carries the resolved path.

## 3. Install from a tag or ref
Sourced (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/install, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference):
- `/plugin marketplace add your-org/plugins#v1.2.0`
- `/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.example.com/your-group/your-marketplace.git#v1.0.0`
- cli-reference also accepts `owner/repo@ref` and `owner/repo#ref`.
- Then install with `/plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace>` or `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> [--scope project]`.
- One-step form, needing v2.1.275 or later in a session and v2.1.292 or later in a shell: `claude plugin install deploy-helper --marketplace your-org/plugins`. The docs show it without a ref, but it accepts the same source forms, so a `#ref` suffix should work. I did not see that exact combination written out.
- A marketplace entry can pin a plugin source in `marketplace.json`: `{"source":"github","repo":"owner/repo","ref":"v2.0.0","sha":"<40-hex>"}`. The same fields exist for `url` and `git-subdir`. When both are set, `sha` wins (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces).
- Marketplace sources support `ref` but not `sha`.
- There is no `/plugin install name@tag` syntax. The tag pins the marketplace repo, or the plugin entry's `ref`.
- The cli-reference page also mentions a command that creates an annotated tag named `<name>--v<version>`. The search excerpt was garbled, so check it before relying on it.

## 4. Material 3
Sourced:
- **Type scale** (https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/type-scale-tokens):
  - 15 baseline styles plus 15 emphasized ones (30 in total). The emphasized set was added in Expressive.
  - The scale runs Display, Headline, Title, Body and Label, each in Large, Medium and Small.
  - It uses a Major Second ratio (1.125) with a base size of 14.
  - The default brand and plain typeface is Roboto.
  - Customize line height and tracking, and avoid changing sizes.
  - Line height varies by language script category.
  - Components do not use the emphasized styles by default.
- **Color roles** (https://m3.material.io/styles/color/roles):
  - There are 26 roles in six groups: primary, secondary, tertiary, error, surface and outline.
  - "On" roles go on the paired fill, and container roles are fills, not for text.
  - Pair the roles as intended.
  - Pairs give at least 3:1 contrast.
  - There are five surface-container roles, from lowest to highest.
  - Contrast levels are standard, medium (3:1 minimum) and high (7:1), in both light and dark (https://m3.material.io/styles/color/system/how-the-system-works).
- **Dark theme:** the dark-theme overview URL returned not found. What I did find: light and dark come from the same roles, and the algorithm assigns tones to each (how-the-system-works page). Dark elevation uses tonal overlays, not shadows alone (https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3). I found no standalone dark-theme page, so treat dark-theme rules as not found beyond this.
- **Motion:**
  - Springs are the default system. The expressive and standard spring tokens are split into spatial and effects.
  - Web conversion curves have durations of 150 to 300 ms for effects and 350 to 750 ms for spatial.
  - The older easing and duration tokens are the fallback (https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/specs).
- **Navigation drawer:** confirmed. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-drawer/overview says "The navigation drawer is no longer recommended in the Material 3 Expressive update" (May 2025). It says to use an expanded navigation rail. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-rail/overview says the expanded rail replaces the drawer and the baseline rail is not recommended. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-rail/guidelines says compact windows always use a navigation bar.

## 5. iOS 27 Liquid Glass changes versus iOS 26
Sourced from Apple:
- https://developer.apple.com/design/whats-new, dated June 8, 2026, lists updated guidance for scroll views (scroll edge effects), sidebars (icon colors), app icons ("refined guidance for Liquid Glass"), tab bars, menus and search fields.
- https://developer.apple.com/ios/whats-new/ says only "Refreshed materials, refined typography, and updated tab and navigation bars".
- The HIG Materials page returned empty content, so I could not read Apple's detailed text.

Sourced from press quoting the WWDC26 keynote (not Apple pages): https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/10/how-liquid-glass-is-changing-in-ios-27/, https://www.cultofmac.com/news/liquid-glass-changes-ios-27-macos-27, https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/08/apple-updates-liquid-glass-ui-in-ios-27-with-new-slider-to-customize-how-it-looks/.
- A system slider in Settings, Appearance, ranges from ultra clear to fully tinted. It replaces the iOS 26 Clear and Tinted options.
- Complex content behind glass is diffused better, and glass has a darkened edge and brighter highlights. Existing apps get this without recompiling.
- A uniform toolbar appears when content scrolls under floating bars, adjustable through the existing scroll-edge APIs.
- App icons are sharper and gain refraction, and Icon Composer 2 adds layered glass.
- Sidebars extend to the window edge and keep corner radii consistent, per the same press coverage.

Sourced from a single third-party designer blog, https://designfornative.com/what-designers-need-to-know-about-ios-27/ (treat as unconfirmed):
- The default scroll-edge style is now hard, and there is no bottom scroll-edge effect unless `.soft` is set.
- Apps built with Xcode 27 can no longer opt out of the glass appearance.
- Dark-mode glass is lighter.
- Default prominent-button label contrast is better.

Unverified: https://gamery.app/blog/liquid-glass/ claims glass-on-glass is now encouraged. It contradicts the iOS 26 HIG rule, and I found no Apple source for it. Do not pin it.

## 6. GitHub rulesets and workflows
Sourced:
- **Ruleset body** (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets`):
  - Top-level fields: `name`, `target:"branch"`, `enforcement:"active"` and `bypass_actors`.
  - Ref condition: `conditions.ref_name.include` and `exclude`.
  - Rule types: `pull_request`, `required_status_checks` and `non_fast_forward`.
  - `pull_request` parameters required: `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push`, `require_code_owner_review`, `require_last_push_approval`, `required_approving_review_count` (0 to 10) and `required_review_thread_resolution`.
  - `required_status_checks` parameters: `strict_required_status_checks_policy` (required) and a `required_status_checks` array of `{context, integration_id?}`.
  - `non_fast_forward` blocks force pushes. It has no parameters.
  - A shape matching these fields appears in https://github.com/digitalnsw/nswds-devops/blob/main/ONBOARDING.md, a third-party repo.
- **Ref patterns** (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/creating-rulesets-for-a-repository): fnmatch with `File::FNM_PATHNAME`, so `*` does not match `/`. `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` and `~ALL` are also accepted. The `include` array takes names or patterns, but I did not see a documented example with the `refs/heads/` prefix. The Web UI and the API accept `refs/heads/...` forms. Verify against the live API before applying.
- **Check names:**
  - The required context is the job's `name:`, or its id when it has none, and a matrix expands per combination. This comes from the third-party tool https://github.com/cntrl-alt-lenny/gx-spirit-caller/blob/b1015c87/tools/check_ci_contract.py. The official page https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks consistently refers to a required `build` job.
  - A job in a reusable workflow reports as `callerJob / calledJob`, per the third-party https://github.com/GSTJ/magic README and nswds-devops. I found no official statement of this.
  - GitHub docs say a check must have run successfully within the past seven days before it can be selected.
  - A workflow skipped by path or branch filters leaves the check pending, which blocks the PR forever. Do not require a check from a filtered workflow.
- **Order the runs:**
  - `workflow_run` with `types: [completed]` and a check of `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` is documented (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows). It fires whatever the upstream conclusion was.
  - It only fires if the workflow file is on the default branch. Its `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF` are the default-branch tip, so use `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`. It supports `branches` filters, and the chain is limited to three levels.
  - Jobs in one workflow with `needs` is the simpler option when both parts can live in one file.
- **Reusable workflows** (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows): they can nest up to ten levels, and a same-repository `./.github/workflows/x.yml` or `$/…` call uses the caller's commit. The docs state no restriction on the caller's trigger event.

Inference:
- A `workflow_run`-triggered workflow can call `workflow_call` workflows. The docs state no restriction, but I found no explicit statement and did not test it.
- The `publish.yml` plan therefore needs a `workflow_run` file on `main` and must check out `head_sha`. The `branches` filter excludes tag pushes, but a `push` trigger needs a test on tags.
- A single workflow with `needs` avoids the default-branch bootstrap problem and the chain limit.
